messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Emma Shaw <emma.shaw@medsys.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@medsys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Success hypotheses, closure conditions & observability — MAP draft

Hi Emma / Alex / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our call, attaching a draft MAP that focuses specifically on defining the success hypotheses (what must be true), the closure/exit conditions (what will move us to pilot/paid), and the acceptance tests (concrete checks we can run). The two attachments are the working MAP spreadsheet and an evidence checklist that lists artifacts you can provide for each acceptance test.

High-level framing:
- Success hypotheses: concise, measurable statements (e.g., 95% intent-match on triage intents, 99.9% uptime during test window, <200ms median inference lat).
- Closure conditions: a short set of pass/fail gates spanning functionality, quality, security, and ops readiness.
- Acceptance tests: reproducible tests with owners, data inputs, expected outputs, and evidence types.

Immediate asks from Medsys:
1) Confirm which three workflows we should prioritize for evaluation (triage, follow-up scheduling, and billing-codes validation are our recommendation).
2) Confirm procurement timeline and any additional vendor evidence you need beyond the checklist (e.g., SOC 2 Type II report, architecture diagram, IP/DSA).
3) Identify internal owners for acceptance-test sign-off.

Proposed dates (editable in attachment):
- Test design & instrumentation (two weeks) — Nov 16–27
- Run acceptance tests (two weeks) — Nov 30–Dec 11
- Decision review & close (one week) — Dec 14–Dec 18

Ben / Karthik / Laura — flagged you for instrumentation/ops, pricing, and legal/security questions respectively. I included brief notes inline in the spreadsheet.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the MAP.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: MAP-draft-v2.xlsx (workbook), evidence-checklist-reqs.pdf (PDF checklist)

From: Dr. Emma Shaw <emma.shaw@medsys.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@medsys.com>, Alex Reyes <alex.reyes@medsys.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Success hypotheses, closure conditions & observability — MAP draft

Jasmine — thanks for the clear draft and the attachments. Quick answers and a few clarifying asks below.

1) Workflows: we agree to prioritize triage and follow-up scheduling. Billing-codes validation is lower priority for phase 1; could be phase 2.
2) Procurement timeline: we need vendor paperwork and evidence by Dec 4 to get on the Dec 10 board packet. Can you confirm you can deliver SOC 2 Type II summary, data retention policy, and an encryption-at-rest statement by Dec 3?
3) Owners: I will own clinical acceptance for triage; Alex will coordinate procurement sign-off. I'll loop in IT security if we need more detail.

One functional note: for the triage acceptance test, we need clarification on how you’ll evaluate distributional drift for our historical 2024–2026 tickets. Do you plan to run drift detection as part of the acceptance suite, or is that post-pilot monitoring?

Can we also add a nonfunctional gate: latency measured from our app edge to response token start — median and 95th across the test corpus? We want to validate end-to-end latency, not only inference time.

Thanks — available Thursday 11/19 09:00–10:00 PT for a quick sync to align owners and timeline.

— Emma
Dr. Emma Shaw
Director, Clinical Operations, Medsys Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Success hypotheses, closure conditions & observability — MAP draft

Jasmine / team — quick operational clarifications to fold into the MAP before Thursday's sync:

- Observability: we'll deliver an instrumentation packet that includes (a) per-route latency histograms (edge->app->inference), (b) token-level cost breakdown, and (c) model confidence buckets for sampled outputs. Ben will own the setup; Karthik will validate cost targets.
- Drift detection: we'll include a lightweight drift check as part of the acceptance tests — it will run on a held-out slice of your 2024–2026 historical tickets with a delta threshold you define. If drift exceeds threshold, the test flags but does not automatically fail; it moves the decision to the risk-review gate.
- Evidence delivery: SOC 2 summary + encryption statement are attached to vendor portal; Laura, can you confirm whether the SOC 2 summary we shared last quarter covers the requirements for Medsys or if we need a new extract?

Notes: the end-to-end latency gate Emma asked for will be measured by us using a synthetic harness that exercises your app edge to ensure reproducible numbers; we will publish median and 95th percentile in the MAP.

Ben
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Emma / Alex / procurement — thanks for the quick responses and the timeline. Finalized updates below and concrete next steps. I've also attached MAP-draft-v2.xlsx with an editable tab called "Acceptance Tests" that enumerates each gate, the pass criteria, the test harness, evidence types, and an owner.

Consolidated acceptance gates (short):
A) Functional correctness — pass = F1 >= 0.86 on the triage validation set (owner: Emma; test: labeled 1k sample). Evidence: labeled test CSV + confusion matrix.
B) End-to-end latency — pass = median <= 280ms and 95th <= 650ms measured from app edge to token start (owner: Ben). Evidence: synthetic harness logs + latency histograms.
C) Reliability & availability — pass = no more than one P1 during test window and observed uptime >= 99.9% (owner: Ben). Evidence: uptime report, incident log.
D) Security/compliance checklist — pass = SOC 2 summary + encryption-at-rest statement + data retention policy (owner: Laura). Evidence: PDF extracts and signed attestations.
E) Observability & rollback readiness — pass = instrumentation deployed and smoke regression test run; defined rollback plan and fallback model variant for degraded performance (owner: Karthik). Evidence: runbook link and canary policy doc.

Drift rule: if drift delta > configured threshold (per the spreadsheet) the gate moves to a risk-review (not automatic fail). Risk-review will include clinical owner + SE + your IT security.

Delivery commitments:
- Redwood will upload SOC 2 summary + encryption statement to the procurement portal by Dec 3 (Laura).
- Instrumentation packet and synthetic harness results (first pass) by Dec 8 (Ben).
- Medsys to provide labeled 1k triage sample and name clinical sign-off owner by Nov 27 (Emma).

Next steps:
- Confirm owners in the spreadsheet and accept the MAP by EOD Monday 11/22 so we can lock dates for test windows.
- If helpful, we can run the Thursday 11/19 slot — otherwise propose Monday 11/23 10:00 PT for a 30-min alignment.

Thanks everyone — attaching the updated MAP and checklist again.

Regards,
Jasmine Liu
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
